newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks seen advancing but upside limited.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks seen advancing but upside limited.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to move sideways with a slight upward bias on Tuesday, limited by weaker trading volume and strong near-term resistance, brokers said.
"We still have some room to go up today," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities. "But resistance lies at 15,500."

On Monday, the Hang Seng Index advanced 145.65 points, or 0.96 percent, to a record close of 15,370.94 after hitting an all-time high of 15,502.54. Overnight, the Hang Seng London Reference Index shed 11.95 points, or 0.08 percent, to 15,358.99.
"But volume levels don't quite reflect this bullishness," said Shum.
Monday's turnover was a hefty HK$19.07 billion, but still much lower than the HK$26 billion levels seen in recent weeks.
Leadership in the market could rotate to banks from utilities and properties, brokers said.
"It looks like the rebound in property counters ended yesterday," said Kenneth Tang, director of Sassoon Futures.
"Banks are likely to do better today, but on the whole I expect the market to move sideways."
